name: FAB / Back-to-Top
summary: Floating action button primitive with hidden and visible states for scroll-triggered actions such as back-to-top.

anatomy.name: icon
anatomy.description: Decorative action icon rendered inside the named button.

behavior.name: controlledVisibility
behavior.description: Visible is a controlled target input. Targets own thresholds, contextual relevance, safe-area/fixed-chrome collision handling, and synchronization; the primitive does not observe scroll.

behavior.name: hiddenFocusExclusion
behavior.description: After the exit transition completes, the hidden base state uses visibility:hidden and cannot receive keyboard or programmatic focus.

behavior.name: action
behavior.description: The named native button emits activation. The target owns the action result, scroll behavior, focus result, and persistence.

behavior.name: motionPreference
behavior.description: Visibility, transform, opacity, and hover transitions are removed when reduced motion is requested; target-owned smooth scrolling must honor the same preference.

properties.name: accessibleLabel
properties.description: Accessible name for the persistent page-level action.

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Decorative icon that visually identifies the page-level action.

properties.name: visible
properties.description: Shows the FAB after target-owned scroll or contextual visibility logic decides it is relevant.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Makes a visible native FAB unavailable without changing target-owned visibility.

accessibility: Provide a clear accessible name for the floating action.
Do not make the FAB the only way to complete critical navigation.
Keep the control reachable by keyboard when visible and excluded from focus after it becomes hidden.
Treat the icon as decorative when the button already has an accessible name.
Use a target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
Honor reduced-motion preferences for visibility and target-owned scrolling.

web.notes: Implemented as a native named button with controlled hidden/visible classes, native disabled/focus behavior, and reduced-motion CSS; visibility thresholds and action effects are target-owned.
